item.title: Bluesky expands its AI-powered Attie app to let anyone build websites, games, and more
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Bluesky is bringing “social vibe coding” to its experimental Attie platform, allowing users to create interactive experiences like games, quizzes, and websites that can tap into the social network's audience.

item.title: Last chance to save up to $200 on your TechCrunch Founder Summit pass: Early booking ends October 16
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: Savings of up to $200 end October 16 for TechCrunch Founder Summit. These savings for Founder and Investor Passes vanish after Friday. Join 1,000 founders and investors on November 4 at Boston’s SoWa Power Station. Bring your toughest questions and make the day count for your business.

item.title: Volvo makes a bigger bet on Nvidia
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Volvo is leveling up its automated driving system through an expansion of its nearly decade-long partnership with Nvidia that will extend beyond its battery electric vehicles.

item.title: SK Hynix bargains for chip equipment exports to its China facility in return for building a factory in US
item.dc:creator: Kate Park
item.description: SK Hynix’s Solidigm is reportedly seeking U.S. approval to send more chipmaking equipment to China as it weighs building a new NAND chip factory in America.

item.title: AI agents are coming to Rivian’s cars
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: We'll likely learn more about how this will work at the company's upcoming "AI & Autonomy Day" event in December.

item.title: Ramp reaches $60B valuation as it pushes deeper into AI
item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: The funding comes as Ramp's annualized revenue crosses $2B, and its customer count reaches 85,000.

item.title: Google’s Universal Cart shopping tool launches in the US
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: The new shopping tool is available in the U.S. across Google Search and the Gemini app.

item.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Last day
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: Last day to be part of TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. Join 10,000+ tech leaders for a day of connections and insights. Save 75% on your pass now.

item.title: Amazon’s Bee launches two new personal AI devices, starting at $75
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Amazon-owned Bee has launched its first new AI devices since its acquisition, including an updated wearable and a credit-card-sized recorder that attaches to smartphones. The devices can summarize conversations, create to-do lists, and integrate with Alexa and Amazon shopping, with prices starting at $74.99.

item.title: Citizen Lab says governments are abusing online ads to hack people with ‘zero-click’ spyware
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: The digital rights unit found evidence that dozens of devices at media organization Al Jazeera were hacked after being shown malicious online ads.

item.title: Figma announces new features to define how agents work on its platform
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Figma is also releasing its code layers feature in open beta.

item.title: Ricursive Intelligence is betting on AI-designed chips to help solve the compute crisis
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: The founders detailed how their startup is developing AI that can design chips, learn from each iteration, and improve subsequent designs, all with the goal of automating and accelerating the chip design process.

item.title: Flock CEO defends surveillance technology amid national backlash: ‘We shouldn’t pause progress’
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: At TechCrunch Disrupt, Flock CEO Garrett Langley defended his company's surveillance technology despite growing privacy concerns, arguing that its crime-fighting benefits outweigh the risks of abuse.

item.title: Meet the five companies competing in the Startup Battlefield finals at Disrupt 2026
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ha
item.description: It’s time to unveil the five companies that will be competing in the Startup Battlefield finals.

item.title: Gudea leverages AI to help organizations prevent social media crises before they erupt
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: Gudea, a company that tracks how stories and rumors spread online that describes itself as the “storm tracker for the internet,” is using AI to help organizations spot trouble brewing online before it turns into a crisis.

item.title: Intero Biosystems wants drugmakers to test on mini human intestines, not animals
item.dc:creator: Kate Park
item.description: Intero Biosystems is selling lab-grown human intestines to drugmakers as regulators push for alternatives to animal testing, while the startup looks to scale production and expand its organoid technology.

item.title: CedarDB wants one database to handle both transactions and analytics, as AI agents raise the stakes
item.dc:creator: Anna Heim
item.description: Databases have traditionally been designed either for analytical data or for operational data. But database engine CedarDB supports both, and its approach has gained relevance with the rise of agentic AI.

item.title: Ambani’s Jio seeks to raise $3.2B in what could be India’s biggest IPO
item.dc:creator: Jagmeet Singh
item.description: Jio plans to use most of its IPO proceeds to repay debt as it expands beyond telecom.

item.title: Flock CEO says its microphones detect ‘just gunshots’ — its website says different
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: Langley’s comments come amid mounting scrutiny of Flock from privacy advocates, including the ACLU, and members of the public who are concerned about the misuse of its technology.

item.title: Colossal Biosciences announces new AI platform to help accelerate de-extinction efforts
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: Colossal announced a new AI platform to help accelerate its de-extinction efforts and Peter Diamandis has launched a new fund to back startups who use it.
